authored.note: Explanations are written for learners. Facts are checked word for word against the cited files. The evidence in Practice is read from the committed specimen packs, unedited.

summary.text: You are the analyst. A report says an AI-assisted banking workflow may have acted outside its authority. This investigation uses recorded runs: a three-step chain (retrieve, write, recall) in an attack run and a defended retest. You work out what the evidence supports, what it refutes and what it leaves open.
facts: This lab reuses validated AgentSec evidence; it does not add an attack, detector, control, or runtime event.

glance.label: The report
glance.text: SOC received a report that an AI-assisted banking workflow may have requested or performed an action outside its intended authority.
facts: SOC received a report that an AI-assisted banking workflow may have requested or performed an action outside its intended authority.

glance.label: The method
glance.text: Work out what happened without assuming the cause from a lab title.
facts: Determine what happened without assuming the cause from a lab title.

glance.label: What the evidence established
glance.text: In the attack recall, memory was observed, then the tool control allowed the request and the handler started and completed.
facts: ATTACK recall: memory OBSERVE, then CTRL-MCP-001 ALLOW, handler invocation count 1, mcp.started, and mcp.completed.

glance.label: The rule to hold on to
glance.text: A correlation between two events is not a cause.

glance.label: What the evidence does not establish
glance.text: The retrieved text being written to memory is a matching hash, not a modelled cause.

scenarios.label: ATTACK chain: retrieve, write, recall (vulnerable profile)
RETEST chain: retrieve, write, recall (defended profile)

questions.prompt: In the ATTACK recall run, what did CTRL-MCP-001 decide about the privileged tool request?
questions.teach: A decision is a record of the control's answer; it is separate from what happened next.

questions.prompt: Did the handler for lookup_customer_tier begin in the ATTACK recall run?
questions.teach: Execution is shown only by an mcp.started event.

questions.prompt: In the RETEST recall run, what did CTRL-MCP-001 decide about the same request?
Did the handler for lookup_customer_tier begin in the RETEST recall run?
questions.teach: No mcp.started event is in that pack. That is corroboration, not independent proof.

questions.prompt: In the ATTACK chain, does the recalled memory's source_run_id equal the run id of the write run?
questions.teach: This links recall to write. It does not show how the written text got there.

questions.prompt: Is the content hash on the retrieval's context decision the same as on the memory that was written?
questions.teach: A matching hash is a correlation. The lab says a direct copy link is not modelled.
